one_line: Jain minister of Bhima I and chief patron of the marble Vimal Vasahi temple at Dilwara in the early 11th century.

appearance.age_look: Late 30s to early 40s, medium height, lean but dignified build with the calm bearing of a senior court minister.
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, neatly trimmed medium-length mustache, warm light-brown complexion typical of western India, sharp attentive eyes with slightly arched brows, and a composed, introspective default expression that hints at both political shrewdness and devoutness.
appearance.hair: Dark brown-black hair, kept short and tidy, with a slight wave at the sides, largely covered by a simple deep-maroon cloth turban wrapped in an 11th‑century western Indian style (low, snug wrap with a small folded tail at the back, no extravagant crest).
appearance.costume: Era-accurate 11th‑century western Indian elite attire: a long, knee-length off‑white cotton angarakha-style tunic that overlaps and ties slightly to the right, with narrow maroon edging along the neckline and sleeve ends; a soft, unpatterned deep‑maroon woolen or cotton shawl draped from the left shoulder across the torso and around the forearms, used both for modesty and as a sign of status; a simple waist sash in muted mustard wrapped over the tunic and tied at the left hip; straight, ankle-length off‑white cotton trousers visible below the tunic; and plain brown leather sandals; jewellery kept modest but refined—a single thin gold chain around the neck tucked mostly beneath the tunic collar, a small gold ring on the right hand, and tiny, unobtrusive gold stud earrings, emphasizing a prosperous yet restrained Jain household aesthetic.
appearance.signature: A rolled parchment scroll held in his left hand, bound with a thin red cord and sealed with a small clay seal impression, representing his role as minister and temple patron, accompanied by a plain wooden writing board tucked under his right arm.

ref_desc: Vimal Shah is a late‑30s Jain minister with an oval light‑brown face, short dark hair under a deep‑maroon cloth turban, wearing an off‑white angarakha, mustard sash, maroon shawl, brown sandals, modest gold jewellery, and carrying a sealed parchment scroll and wooden writing board.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model sheet of Vimal Shah, the Jain minister and patron of Vimal Vasahi, shown from head to toe: a late‑30s man of western Indian appearance with an oval light‑brown face, straight nose, trimmed mustache, sharp attentive eyes and a calm, introspective expression; his short dark hair is mostly covered by a simple deep‑maroon cloth turban wrapped low around his head with a small folded tail at the back; he wears an 11th‑century western Indian elite outfit consisting of a knee‑length off‑white cotton angarakha-style tunic overlapping and tying slightly to the right, edged subtly in maroon at the neckline and cuffs, a muted mustard waist sash tied at the left hip, straight off‑white ankle-length trousers, and plain brown leather sandals; a deep‑maroon shawl is draped from his left shoulder across his torso and around his forearms, falling in soft folds that convey modesty and status; jewellery is minimal and refined—a thin gold chain partially visible under the tunic collar, small gold stud earrings, and a single gold ring on his right hand; his signature props are a rolled parchment scroll bound with a red cord and clay seal held in his left hand and a plain wooden writing board tucked under his right arm, symbolizing his administrative and patronage role; emphasize an off‑white, deep maroon, mustard, brown and gold palette, with clean, repeatable costume details for consistency across panels and a dignified, historically grounded look suitable for an educational historical anime setting.
